title: M151 · Team Companion identity, R0 (three treatments drawn; not finished, CI red)
summary: R0 drew three candidate identities for Team Companion and put each on the landing page (1280 and 390), a shared plan (390) and Match Day (390): T1 a ruled field sketch of the map, T2 an engraved contour sheet, T3 a schematic. Also built: nine original marks for the five roles and objectives (atelier PASS after fixes, in the /design gallery), a reMarkable template if you want to draw them yourself, the lock-in motion for a draft pick (fixed at 390 after critique), a static win/loss stamp, three Open Graph link cards plus a favicon candidate, and a 'paper' light still of the share page. All of it is gallery and planning files; nothing reached the app's real pages or production. NOT done: the atelier's fixes for T1 are written but not applied (the T1 stills you see are BEFORE those fixes; the critique said it reads as 'a square with an X'); T2, T3, the OG cards and the paper still have no atelier critique yet; the lock-in 1280 strip predates the fix; CI is red (Clippy on the SSR build has failed since the marks gallery section). The round stopped at its 5.0 M budget cap. One legal question for your adviser: may a fan tool draw its own role/objective marks that resemble in-game icons? Ours are original geometry, deliberately distant. Report: REPORT-R0.md.

questions.text: Which treatment should carry the identity (react)? Note: the T1 stills are pre-fix; the atelier wrote a fix list (straight lanes, one curved river, lighter hatch, a proper Match Day inset) that R0b would apply.

chips.label: T1 field sketch
chips.consequence: R0b applies the atelier's T1 fixes, re-renders and gets a fresh critique; T2 and T3 are dropped.

chips.label: T2 contour
chips.consequence: R0b takes the engraved contour sheet forward: first atelier critique, then fixes; T1 and T3 dropped.

chips.label: T3 schematic
chips.consequence: R0b takes the schematic forward: first atelier critique, then fixes; T1 and T2 dropped.

questions.recommend: T1 field sketch, with the atelier's fixes. It is the only one that says 'League team' without words once the lanes are straight and the river curves, and it is the only one already critiqued.

questions.text: Role and objective marks (react): draw them yourself on the reMarkable template, or take the nine marks the atelier passed?

chips.label: Draw them myself (reMarkable template)
chips.consequence: You draw nine marks on marks-template.pdf; IMPORT.md turns them into public/marks/*.svg, then an atelier check at 16 px.

chips.label: Take the atelier set
chips.consequence: The nine drawn marks ship as they are (after the legal answer and the DESIGN amendment).

questions.recommend: Take the atelier set. It passed at 16 px beside its word; your hand can replace single marks later through the same template.

questions.text: Lead-figure grammar (react): one figure, one sentence, one action on landing, share and Match Day. Adopt it as the page rule?

chips.label: Yes
chips.consequence: DESIGN.md gets the rule; R1 rebuilds the three surfaces around it.

chips.label: No
chips.consequence: Pages keep today's layout; the identity is applied as art only.

questions.recommend: Yes. It is what makes the stills read in a second, and it matches the one-primary-action rule already in DESIGN.

questions.text: C paper still (react): a light 'paper' version of the share page. Does it convince you enough to plan a light theme?

chips.label: Convinced
chips.consequence: A later round plans a paper theme; chalk becomes deep olive and the danger hover rule changes.

chips.label: Not convinced
chips.consequence: One dark theme stays; the still is archived.

questions.recommend: Not convinced, for now. It costs a rule change and a second token set, and it has had no critique yet.
